items.title: Joint Business Case, Not a Construction Date, Anchors Crombie's Subway Pitch for Mississauga
items.summary: CityNews Toronto reports Mississauga mayoral candidate Bonnie Crombie has unveiled a plan to push for a western extension of the TTC's Line 2 subway into the city, starting with a joint business case rather than a construction commitment. According to the outlet, Crombie says she would work with the province, Metrolinx, the City of Toronto and the TTC to study extending the line west from Kipling Station through Sherway Gardens and into Mississauga's city centre. The outlet reports the proposal includes no construction timeline or cost estimate, focusing instead on determining whether the project is feasible and how it could be delivered. CityNews says Crombie, if elected, would convene meetings with government and transit partners within her first 100 days and seek federal involvement in the planning process, while also bringing a council motion in that same window to formally launch the city's participation and identify funding for its share. According to the proposal, the study would examine potential routes and station locations, including options near Sherway Gardens and City Centre, along with connections to the Hazel McCallion Line, GO Transit, MiWay and the Mississauga Transitway. The outlet reports the study would also look at ridership, travel-time savings, accessibility, nearby housing and employment growth, construction and operating costs, and environmental impacts. CityNews says Crombie wants the jointly funded study underway within her first year in office, with the initial business case completed within two years.

items.title: October 26 Marks Election Day for Mississauga's Mayor, Council and School Trustees
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, residents head to the polls on Monday, Oct. 26, to elect the city's next mayor, their ward and regional councillor, and local school board trustees for the 2026 to 2030 term. The city says voters can cast a ballot at any voting location within their own ward rather than being tied to a single assigned site. Officials recommend confirming you're on the voters' list before heading out, since that step can speed up the process at the polls. Anyone who received a voter notification card in September is encouraged to bring it along, though the city notes the card isn't required to vote. What is required, according to the city, is one piece of identification showing your name and a qualifying Mississauga address. The City of Mississauga says it remains committed to accessible voting, and residents looking for details on accommodations can find them through the Ways to Vote page on the city's Mississauga Votes site.

items.title: Displacement Fears at Twin Pines Mobile Home Park Dominate Ward 3 Election Platforms
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports that long-standing fears over displacement at the Twin Pines Mobile Home Park are dominating candidate platforms in Ward 3 ahead of the Oct. 26 municipal election. According to the outlet, Peel Region is moving ahead with plans to redevelop the Dundas Street East property into affordable housing, a site that once held more than 200 homes and now has roughly 130 remaining as residents weigh Peel Living's exit offer. The outlet reports many of the long-term residents are seniors on fixed incomes with few options to buy a new home, leaving them looking to their next municipal representative, who also holds a seat at Peel Regional Council, for clear transition commitments. Mississauga.com says candidates responded to the issue, along with other hot-button concerns like road safety and density, in emailed statements. Candidate Fonseca told the outlet she has advocated for Twin Pines residents since 2010 and will keep doing so at Peel Regional Council, adding that building more affordable housing elsewhere does not erase the city's responsibility toward residents already there. According to Mississauga.com, Fonseca called for individualized assistance, clear information and appropriate housing choices for those being displaced, saying success should be measured by how well the community is supported through the transition.

items.title: Driver Remained at Scene After Child Struck on Hillcrest Avenue in Cooksville, Police Say
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say a child was struck by a vehicle Monday afternoon in Mississauga's Cooksville neighbourhood. According to police, the incident happened on Hillcrest Avenue near Confederation Parkway, just north of Dundas Street East. CTV News reports the driver remained at the scene after the collision. Police told the outlet the child was taken to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. According to police, the investigation is ongoing, and anyone with further information is asked to contact Peel police or Crime Stoppers.

items.title: Peel Public Health Opens Respiratory Vaccine Clinics in Mississauga Starting This Week
items.summary: Insauga.com reports Peel Public Health is opening vaccination clinics this week as officials urge residents to protect themselves against flu, COVID-19 and RSV ahead of the colder months. According to the outlet, appointments for high-risk and priority groups begin Wednesday, Oct. 21, with vaccines opening to the general population aged six months and older on Monday, Oct. 26. The outlet reports both clinics are located at 7120 Hurontario St. in Mississauga, serving residents of Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon. Peel's Medical Officer of Health, Dr. Alexa Caturay, said vaccination is an important way for residents to protect themselves and their families as people spend more time indoors and respiratory viruses spread more easily. According to Insauga.com, health officials say the shots do not eliminate the chance of infection but can lower the risk of serious illness, particularly for older adults, young children and pregnant people.

items.title: Streetsville's Final Fall Walking Tour Retraces the Night a Crowd Silenced Solomon Northup in 1857
items.summary: Insauga.com reports the final Streetsville Historic Walking Tour of the 2026 season, set for Wednesday, Oct. 21, will focus on Solomon Northup, whose memoir Twelve Years a Slave inspired the Oscar-winning 2013 film of the same name. According to the outlet, the tour will revisit Northup's visit to Streetsville in August 1857, when a hostile crowd prevented him from speaking about his experiences at what is now Streetsville Village Square. The outlet reports the tour is led by local historian Richard Collins, who guided the village's walking tours throughout the year. Insauga.com says Northup was born a free man in New York around 1807, kidnapped and sold into slavery in 1841, and endured 12 years of enslavement in Louisiana before regaining his freedom in 1853 and publishing his memoir. According to the outlet, Northup travelled to Canada four years later to lecture about slavery with support from the Anti-Slavery Society of Canada, a trip that brought him to Streetsville.
